finalText:
All 10 failures involve a percent coupon, and only in currencies converted from USD at a non-trivial rate — confirms the bug is in `computeTotal` in `engine.js:23-31`.

It rounds the USD subtotal to 2 decimal places right after applying the percent coupon (and again after the flat coupon), then converts that already-rounded number to the order's currency. The test's reference total does the math in full precision and rounds only once, at the very end, after converting to the target currency. Those two extra roundings happen to cancel out for USD and EUR, but for GBP, CAD, and JPY the rate multiplication turns that hidden penny of rounding error into a visible one, so the cart lands a cent (or a yen) off — exactly the "some carts are off, most look fine" pattern finance flagged.

Fix: round only once, after `convert()`, and drop the intermediate `round()` calls on the USD subtotal.
